name: Airbnb
one_liner: Marketplace letting people rent out spare rooms and homes to travelers.
story: Founded in 2008 as AirBed & Breakfast, the idea of paying to sleep on a stranger's air mattress was dismissed by most investors; in June 2008 seven investors were offered 10% for $150,000 and none bit, and the founders kept the company alive by selling Obama O's and Cap'n McCain's cereal (about $30,000) before Y Combinator and Sequoia backed them in 2009. After a $31B private valuation fell to about $18B when COVID-19 crushed travel and it took a high-interest $1B Silver Lake/Sixth Street lifeline in April 2020, Airbnb IPO'd on Nasdaq in December 2020 at $68 (about $47B fully diluted) and closed day one at $144.71 for a roughly $86.5B market cap (peak_valuation_usd uses that first-day cap; later intraday highs not verified).

near_death.what: Out of money and in credit card debt, founders sold ~800 boxes of novelty election cereal (Obama O's, Cap'n McCain's) at $40 each, netting about $30,000.
COVID-19 collapsed bookings; Airbnb took $1B in debt and equity from Silver Lake and Sixth Street at over 10% interest as its valuation reportedly fell from $31B to $18B.

dismissed_by.quote_or_fact: Fact: offered 10% of the company for $150,000 (a $1.5M valuation); five sent rejection emails and two never replied, per Brian Chesky's 2015 post '7 Rejections'.
"They have an interesting business. I'm just not sure how big it's going to be."
Paraphrase: USV passed because it could not picture air mattresses on living-room floors becoming a substitute for hotel rooms; Wilson later kept the cereal boxes as a reminder of the miss.

name: Stripe
one_liner: Developer-first API for accepting and moving money online.
story: Founded in 2010 in Palo Alto by Irish brothers Patrick and John Collison (then about 21 and 19), Stripe set out to rebuild online payments, a field dominated by banks, processors and PayPal, as a few lines of developer code, backed by Y Combinator and a $2M round from Peter Thiel, Elon Musk, Sequoia and Andreessen Horowitz. It climbed to a $95B private valuation in 2021, reset to $50B in its 2023 $6.5B Series I, then hit $106.7B and $159B (peak, private, February 2026 tender offer led by Thrive, Coatue and a16z) while staying private. Total raised of ~$9.4B is CB Insights' tally; trackers range from $8.1B to $9.8B.

name: Canva
one_liner: Browser-based drag-and-drop design platform that makes graphic design easy for non-designers.
story: Melanie Perkins, Cliff Obrecht and Cameron Adams launched Canva in Australia in 2012 out of Perkins and Obrecht's Perth yearbook-design business Fusion Books; Perkins was rejected by about 100 VCs, wary of a design startup from Perth taking on Adobe, and it took roughly three years to land the first investment, a $3.6M seed in 2013 (Matrix Partners, InterWest, 500 Startups; reported figure, currency not confirmed). Canva hit $40B in a $200M September 2021 round and $42B in an August 2025 employee share sale (peak_valuation_usd, private; a SmartCompany claim of a $65B peak could not be verified), before investors Blackbird and Airtree marked it down to about $34.9B in August 2026, with an IPO targeted for 2027. Total raised is unresolved: trackers range from $597M (Multiples.vc) to $979M (CB Insights).

dismissed_by.quote_or_fact: Fact: Perkins was rejected by roughly 100 VCs and took about three years to land Canva's first investment.
